intro: Works out the ideal front/rear brake balance from weight transfer, and the deceleration you can really reach with your setting.
cg_hint: Road car ≈ 450–550 mm, race car ≈ 300–400 mm
decel_hint: ≈ tyre grip: road 0.8–1.0 g, semi-slick 1.1–1.3 g, slick 1.4 g and up
bias_hint: Share of braking force at the front

r.optimal_note: All 4 wheels at the limit together at {a} g
r.distance_note: From {s}, without reaction time; ideal setting: {d}
r.inner_front: Inside front wheel in a corner

lock.front: Front wheels lock first ({e}% of potential)
lock.rear: Rear wheels lock first: unstable ({e}% of potential)
lock.both: Both axles reach the limit together ({e}% of potential)

warn.rear_lock: Too much rear braking: the rear locks before the front and the car may spin. Move the balance forward.
warn.front_bias: Setting clearly front-biased: stable car but longer stopping distances and overworked front tyres.
warn.high_cg: High centre of gravity for the wheelbase: large load transfer, the rear goes very light under braking.
warn.unbalanced: Unusual weight distribution: check the corner weights.
warn.wheel_lift: An inside wheel lifts at this lateral acceleration: risk of lock-up and loss of traction.

setup.street: Road setup: keep some front margin for stability (+3 to +5 points).
setup.sport: Sport / semi-slick setup: aim for the ideal ±2 points, adjust with the bias valve.
setup.track: Track / slick setup: aim for the ideal, then fine-tune on track (front lock-up = move the balance rearward).

chart.lateral_title: Load per wheel cornering at {g} g
